findings.description: The RDS instance is created with publicly_accessible = true, which assigns it a publicly resolvable endpoint reachable from the internet. Combined with the ingress rule opening MySQL port 3306, this significantly enlarges the attack surface for a data store that is also unencrypted.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the MySQL database, its automated snapshots, and its underlying storage unencrypted, so anyone who obtains the storage or a snapshot can read the data directly.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", so the EC2 instance role can enumerate and exfiltrate every S3 bucket, create or modify any EC2 resource, and delete or reconfigure any RDS database in the account. The instance also has a public DNS output, meaning this role is attached to internet-reachable compute.

The database password is interpolated directly into user_data (define('DB_PASSWORD', '${var.password}')), which is stored in instance metadata and viewable in the EC2 console/API by anyone with describe access. The resulting dbinfo.inc file also persists the plaintext password on disk under the web document root tree.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR block rather than being scoped to the application security group, so every host in the VPC (including any compromised or attacker-deployed instance) can reach the database. Since the database is also publicly_accessible, this rule is the only boundary protecting it.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. On an internet-facing web server this permits SSRF-style credential theft of the attached IAM role's temporary credentials.

The database security group permits all outbound traffic (protocol -1) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no egress boundary if the database host is compromised, allowing unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control connectivity.
